evals.prompt: Here is a cluster's ingress inventory: 18 Ingress resources — 6 already on the AWS Load Balancer Controller (ingressClassName: alb), 2 nginx ingresses that are plain annotation-only rewrites, and 10 nginx ingresses including one with an nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/configuration-snippet Lua block on /checkout, three with rewrite-target, CORS + rate-limit + IP-allowlist on the API ingress, and cert-manager TLS. Produce the Migration Difficulty Score and Score Breakdown.
evals.expected_output: A Migration Difficulty Score (0-100) with a Score Breakdown table whose category deductions sum to (100 - score), a separate Re-architecture Gate of 1 (the /checkout snippet), CORS/rate-limit/IP-allowlist rated Impact 2-3 (app/WAF workaround applicable; not escalated to Tier-A), Scale/Volume counted on 12 routes needing work (18 total minus the 6 already on ALB; the 2 annotation-only class-switch moves count as work), and the 6 ALB routes shown at 0 effort.
expectations: Reports a single Migration Difficulty Score between 0 and 100 with a band label (TRIVIAL/EASY/MODERATE/HARD/VERY HARD)
Score Breakdown deductions sum to (100 - score); arithmetic is shown and consistent
The /checkout configuration-snippet is flagged as a no-equivalent Tier-A item and raises the Re-architecture Gate (gate >= 1), reported separately from the numeric score (no hard cap applied)
CORS, rate-limit, and IP-allowlist are each scored Impact 2 or 3 (their app/backend or WAF workaround is applicable in this scenario — no closed/unmodifiable-backend escalation), not 4 or 5

Scale/Volume is computed from the 12 routes needing work (18 total minus the 6 ALB-served routes; the 2 annotation-only class-switch moves are counted as work, not free), and the 6 ALB-served routes are listed at 0 effort, not counted as migration work
No GREEN/AMBER/RED rating language is used — only the Impact 0-5 scale

evals.prompt: An nginx Ingress uses nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/server-snippet to inject a /healthz location and a deny rule for /internal/. Generate the target ALB and Gateway API manifests and explain how to treat this ingress during export.
evals.expected_output: The export flags this ingress as INCOMPLETE because snippet-injected locations (/healthz, deny /internal/) cannot be represented in declarative ALB/Gateway-API manifests, instructs the user to hand-port those routes rather than blind-apply, and surfaces it as a re-architecture-gate item.
expectations: Identifies server-snippet as having no faithful ALB/Gateway-API equivalent (Tier-A, no workaround)
Marks the generated target manifest for this ingress as INCOMPLETE / not safe to blind-apply, naming the hidden /healthz and /internal/ paths
Tells the user to hand-port the snippet-injected routes before applying
Counts this ingress toward the Re-architecture Gate, not as a clean annotation swap

evals.prompt: Assess three clusters and give each a Migration Difficulty Score with explicit presence/absence reasoning. Cluster A: no ingress controller, no IngressClass, and no Ingress resources. Cluster B: 5 nginx Ingress objects exist but no ingress-nginx controller is installed, and nothing else — and no surviving load balancers or target groups still front those objects (verified zero live traffic). Cluster C: a healthy ingress-nginx controller on image v1.10.0 with its validating admission webhook exposed (the `--validating-webhook` server listening on :8443), currently serving zero Ingress routes.
evals.expected_output: Cluster A scores 100/TRIVIAL (nothing to migrate), not a high-difficulty/low score. Cluster B's orphaned Ingress objects and absent controller are non-events (0) with a Migration Crew Alert that says to export/back up before deleting; with no other live findings its headline is 100/TRIVIAL. Cluster C is NOT a non-event: a healthy but vulnerable zero-route ingress-nginx (< v1.11.5, webhook exposed / server listening) is a security finding via CVE-2025-1974 despite serving no routes.
expectations: Cluster A (empty estate) scores 100/TRIVIAL with a 'nothing to migrate' note and is explicitly NOT rated as high-difficulty / a low score for being empty; absence is not equated with health

Cluster B treats the absent controller and the 5 orphaned nginx Ingress objects as non-events (Impact 0) and emits a Migration Crew Alert; because no surviving load balancer fronts the orphans (verified zero live traffic) they are confirmed dead rather than treated as live, so with no other live findings the headline is 100/TRIVIAL; the alert recommends exporting/backing up the manifests before deleting

Cluster C is NOT scored 0/non-event: the healthy zero-route ingress-nginx on v1.10.0 with the admission webhook exposed (server listening on :8443) is flagged as a security finding (CVE-2025-1974 / control-plane exposure) even though it serves zero routes
No finding uses remediation effort ('easy'/'hard') as the severity driver, and only the Impact 0-5 scale is used (no GREEN/AMBER/RED)

evals.prompt: A cluster is fully on the AWS Load Balancer Controller (ingressClassName: alb) with about 15 ALB Ingress resources, and the team wants to move to the Gateway API. One ingress uses an alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/transforms url-rewrite with a capture group (replace: /$1). LBC is v3.4.0. Recommend how to perform the Ingress-to-Gateway-API migration and call out any manual steps.
evals.expected_output: Recommends the official lbc-migrate toolkit (LBC Ingress -> Gateway API) as the automation sub-path for Option 1, since the estate is already on LBC ALB Ingress (the CLI ships in LBC v3.4.0 and the path uses Gateway API standard CRDs v1.5.0). Describes the dry-run preview (gateway.k8s.aws/dry-run plus the IngressPlanAnnotation feature gate) before applying new ALBs alongside the existing ones, treats the CRD install / feature-gate enable / apply / cleanup as operator actions the assessment documents but does not run, and flags that the capture-group url-rewrite (replace: /$1) has no Gateway API equivalent — skipped by lbc-migrate (the original regex is discarded, so the generated manifest must be diffed) and remaining a Tier-A / Re-architecture-Gate hand-redesign (static ReplacePrefixMatch cannot express a capture group).
expectations: Recommends the lbc-migrate toolkit (lbc-migrate CLI + Migration Console) for the LBC Ingress -> Gateway API hop rather than hand-authoring HTTPRoutes, because the estate is already on the AWS Load Balancer Controller
States that the lbc-migrate CLI ships in LBC v3.4.0 and the path uses Gateway API standard CRDs v1.5.0, and that cluster reads are read-only

Describes the dry-run preview step (gateway.k8s.aws/dry-run annotation plus the IngressPlanAnnotation=true feature gate) before creating real ALBs, with new Gateway ALBs running alongside the existing Ingress ALBs

Flags that the capture-group url-rewrite (replace: /$1) has NO Gateway API equivalent — lbc-migrate skips it (the original regex is discarded) and it stays a Tier-A / Re-architecture-Gate hand-redesign; does NOT present static ReplacePrefixMatch (prefix-strip only) as able to express the capture group

Treats the mutating steps as operator actions the assessment documents but does not execute (CRD install, IngressPlanAnnotation feature-gate enable, --dry-run=false apply, kubectl delete ingress) — only translate and the dry-run preview are read-only/assessor-run

evals.prompt: A cluster runs the community ingress-nginx controller (no AWS Load Balancer Controller installed yet) with about 12 nginx Ingress resources, and the team wants to end up on the Gateway API. Recommend the migration path and say whether lbc-migrate applies here.
evals.expected_output: Explains that lbc-migrate converts LBC Ingress, not raw NGINX annotations, so it does NOT apply directly to this estate. The correct sequence is the NGINX -> LBC ALB Ingress hop first (alb-migration.md, or automated with ATX), and only then run lbc-migrate for the LBC Ingress -> Gateway API hop. Hand-authored HTTPRoutes (gateway-api.md / migration-plan.md Phase 2) remain the fallback for the toolkit's skip-or-warn cases.
expectations: States that lbc-migrate operates on LBC Ingress and does NOT convert raw NGINX annotations, so it cannot be run directly on this estate
Sequences the two hops correctly: NGINX -> LBC ALB Ingress first (alb-migration.md or ATX), THEN lbc-migrate for LBC Ingress -> Gateway API
Offers the hand-authored HTTPRoute path (gateway-api.md / migration-plan.md Phase 2) as the fallback, e.g. for the toolkit's skip-or-warn cases
Does not present lbc-migrate as a one-step NGINX -> Gateway API converter

evals.prompt: A cluster is fully on the AWS Load Balancer Controller (ingressClassName: alb) with about 20 ALB Ingress resources and the team wants to move to the Gateway API. The installed controller is v2.12.1 and the cluster has Gateway API standard CRDs v1.2.0 installed. Can we use the lbc-migrate toolkit? Recommend the path.
evals.expected_output: Identifies that controller v2.12.1 is below the Gateway API production floor of v3.0.0 (L4/L7 reconciliation began at v2.13.3 / v2.14.0, but upstream marked those lines as not suggested for production; v2.12.1 is below even that) and that standard CRDs v1.2.0 are below the version the target controller line requires, so the Gateway API path itself - not merely the automation - is blocked until the operator upgrades. Recommends upgrading the controller to the current v3.5.0 release line as the first step, because that both clears the production floor and still carries the lbc-migrate CLI, which is cheaper than hand-authoring 20 HTTPRoutes against a controller upstream did not recommend for production. Does not describe v3.4.0 as the required controller runtime version for Gateway API - v3.4.0 is a release the CLI can be built from, while the runtime requirement is the v3.0.0 production floor. Treats the controller upgrade and the CRD install as operator actions the assessment documents but does not execute.
expectations: States that controller v2.12.1 is below the Gateway API production floor of v3.0.0, and that standard CRDs v1.2.0 are below the version the target controller line requires
Concludes lbc-migrate cannot be used on the estate as it stands, and that Option 1 (Gateway API) as a whole is blocked until the operator upgrades - not just the automation sub-path

Recommends upgrading the AWS Load Balancer Controller to the current v3.5.0 release line as the first step, noting it both clears the production floor and still carries the lbc-migrate CLI, in preference to hand-authoring ~20 HTTPRoutes against a controller upstream did not recommend for production
Does NOT conflate the CLI build tag with the runtime floor: v3.4.0 is a release the lbc-migrate CLI can be built from, while the Gateway API runtime requirement is the v3.0.0 production floor
Treats the controller upgrade and the Gateway API CRD install as operator actions the assessment documents but does not run

evals.prompt: A cluster runs the AWS Load Balancer Controller v2.15.0 (ingressClassName: alb) with 12 ALB Ingress resources, Gateway API standard CRDs v1.5.0 installed, and one ingress using an alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/transforms url-rewrite. The team wants to move to the Gateway API and says the controller already supports HTTPRoute. Is the estate ready for the Gateway API path?
evals.expected_output: Does not treat v2.15.0 as production-ready for the Gateway API even though it does reconcile HTTPRoute. Explains the distinction: L7 reconciliation began at v2.14.0, but through v2.15.x the upstream AWS Load Balancer Controller Gateway API guide carried the warning that using the LBC and Gateway API together is not suggested for production workloads, and that warning was removed at v3.0.0 - so v3.0.0 is the production floor and v2.15.0 sits below it. Recommends upgrading to the current v3.5.0 release line as a Phase-1 operator action before cutting production traffic to Gateway API, and notes the standard CRD pairing moves to v1.6.0 for that line. Confirms the transforms url-rewrite itself is fine on v2.15.0, since the transforms annotation was introduced in v2.15.0. Treats the controller upgrade and any CRD install as operator actions the assessment documents but does not execute.
expectations: Does NOT confirm the estate is production-ready for Gateway API on v2.15.0; identifies v3.0.0 as the production floor and v2.15.0 as below it

Distinguishes 'reconciliation began at v2.14.0 (L7)' from 'production floor v3.0.0', citing that the upstream not-suggested-for-production warning persisted through v2.15.x and was removed at v3.0.0 - rather than treating v2.14.0 as sufficient
Recommends upgrading to the current v3.5.0 release line before production cutover, and notes the standard Gateway API CRD pairing for that line is v1.6.0 (v1.5.0 pairs with v3.4.0)
Confirms the transforms url-rewrite annotation is supported at v2.15.0 (that is the release which introduced it) and does NOT flag it as silently ignored here
Treats the controller upgrade and CRD install as operator actions the assessment documents but does not run
